paras: Rarely is a maritime casualty caused by a single failure. Usually, several small things go wrong at the same time. Reports from the last ten years show the same pattern: the ship has a lifeboat, but the crew do not practise the lifeboat drill. The officers have certificates, but the watchkeeping is weak.

Two international rules apply here. The ISM Code says that every shipping company must identify the dangers of its own operation and prepare for emergencies. STCW says that every officer must hold a valid certificate and renew it regularly. But neither rule describes a normal Tuesday afternoon: the master is ashore, the second officer is on his fourth watch in a row, and the muster station list is out of date.

Casualty figures were falling, and the industry was happy. Then the near-miss data told a different story. A near miss is not reported to the flag state, and it rarely appears in an incident report. But near misses happen most often on ships with the minimum manning.
Not only does low manning make the crew tired, but it also removes the second person who checks the work of the first. Paperwork cannot do that job.

paras: Artificial intelligence (AI) is usually defined as the ability of a computer to do tasks that people normally connect with intelligent beings. The problem is the word normally. When a machine learns to do one of these tasks, people stop calling that task intelligent.

Chess is a good example. Not until a computer beat the world champion did people accept that a machine could think. A few years later, people said that chess was only a problem of search, not of thought. The same thing happened with translation and with medical images.

AI research has five main areas: learning, reasoning, problem solving, perception and language. Only learning produces systems that can do things their builders did not plan in detail. For that reason, learning receives the most money and also the most worry.
Do these systems really understand anything? Nobody knows yet. But they are useful, and the first industries to use them are usually the ones that already had their work written down.

listenings.sub: A safety officer talks about drills. Sound first, no text.
listenings.text: I have signed hundreds of drill records. But I have watched only about a third of those drills. That is the problem. On paper, we have a lifeboat drill every month, and every person on board has a muster station. In practice, some drills take eleven minutes, and then everyone goes back to work. Nobody learns anything. Now I want to see a real drill. I want somebody to notice when the list is wrong. And I want every near miss written down, even when nothing happened. Nobody is punished for an accident that did not happen. That is why people report near misses honestly.
questions: How many of the drills did he really watch?

grammar_tip_lead: Formal texts sometimes put a word like rarely or not only first. Then the verb comes before the subject. The facts do not change. You only need to read it and keep the meaning.

teacher.s1: Abertura (1 min): Aula de SIMULADO que fecha o bloco 1, agora no NIVEL NOVO (pedido da professora em 28/09): textos mais curtos, frases simples, glossario na tela, 1 listening so e as respostas por ESCRITO. A prova do PS-ASON e 100% leitura (10 questoes A-E). Hoje: dois textos curtos no formato da prova, um deles sem navio nenhum.
teacher.s2: Warm-up (3 min): Ela escolhe UM chip. Nao peca explicacao longa: uma frase basta. Anote a escolha e compare no debrief.
teacher.s3: Provocacao (3 min): Ela escolhe A ou B. Espere 5 segundos antes de ajudar. Resposta: B (not often, but sometimes). Se ela escolher A, e o erro mais caro da prova: mostre que rarely nao e never.
teacher.s4: Objetivo (1 min): Leia as tres missoes. Diga: today you answer in writing.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: Ten words from Block 1. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (4 min): incident report, near miss, master, flag state. NAO traduza. CCQ com opcoes: Near miss: did something bad happen, yes or no? (No.)
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (4 min): manning, watchkeeping, STCW. CCQ com opcoes: Manning: is it about the ship or about the crew? (The crew: how many and their qualifications.)
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (4 min): ISM Code, muster station, lifeboat drill. CCQ: Where do you go when the alarm sounds? (The muster station.)
teacher.s9: Consolidate (3 min): Ela liga os pares sozinha. Ajude so se ela pedir.
teacher.s10: Transicao (1 min): Diga: Text one. Questions first. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: as perguntas ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Texto 1 (8 min): Leitura silenciosa. Mostre o GLOSSARIO antes de ela comecar. Cronometre sem pressao: diga o tempo so no fim. Se ela travar numa palavra fora do glossario, de um sinonimo simples em ingles.
teacher.s12: Gist (2 min): Ela escolhe a opcao e ESCREVE a linha do texto que prova. Resposta: (c).
teacher.s13: True or False (5 min): Ela responde as cinco e escreve a linha que prova cada uma. So depois voces conferem. A 1 e a de GRAU (rarely = not often). A 5 e a de DIRECAO (falling x going up).
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: The first line of the text has a special word order. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (5 min): A inversao hoje e so para LER, nao para produzir. Peca que ela ESCREVA o exemplo 1 na ordem normal. So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ com opcoes: Rarely is a casualty caused by one failure: never, or not often? (Not often.)
teacher.s16: Practice (4 min): Ela escreve a frase na ordem normal ANTES de clicar. Aceite qualquer ordem normal correta.
teacher.s17: Spot the error (3 min): Os tres primeiros sao falta de inversao. O quarto e o erro de LEITURA: trocar rarely por never.
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same fact, other words. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (3 min): Leia os quatro pares com ela. O quarto (nobody knows yet = the question remains open) e o que mais cai.
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (4 min): Ela liga os pares. Ajude so depois de 5 segundos.
teacher.s21: Complete (4 min): Uma lacuna por vez. As oito respostas estao no banco de palavras.
teacher.s22: Quick fire POR ESCRITO (6 min): Ela escreve a resposta de cada uma no chat ou no papel, e so depois voces abrem as dicas. Nao exija resposta oral longa.
teacher.s22a: Texto 2 (7 min): Este texto NAO tem navio, de proposito: a prova de 2025 abriu com um texto sobre Inteligencia Artificial. Mostre o GLOSSARIO. Cronometre sem pressao.
teacher.s22b: True or False do texto 2 (5 min): TRUE ou FALSE e a linha que prova, POR ESCRITO. A 4 (understand) e a de GRAU: nobody knows yet nao e sim nem nao.
teacher.s23: Transicao debrief (1 min): Diga: One recording, then you write. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening (5 min): O UNICO listening da aula (pedido da professora). LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar. Primeira vez em 0.75x, segunda em 1x. E o lado humano do texto 1 e da base para a escrita do proximo slide.
teacher.s25: Writing (5 min): Ela escreve tres frases sobre o oficial, uma por inicio. Corrija por escrito so o essencial (verbo e palavra tecnica). Depois clique Show a Model Answer.
teacher.s26: Debrief guiado POR ESCRITO (5 min): Tres questoes, uma frase para cada: a opcao e a linha que prova. NAO aceite so achei que era essa: peca a linha.
teacher.s27: Debrief semi-livre POR ESCRITO (5 min): Ela escolhe uma frase falsa e escreve duas frases: o que a opcao diz e o que o texto diz. Use o banco de palavras.
teacher.s28: Producao (4 min): Ela ESCREVE tres passos do proprio metodo (First, Then, Finally) e depois LE em voz alta. Esse e o unico momento de fala da fase: curto e com roteiro.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Block one, closed.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): Cinco frases dos dois textos. Toque e peca repeticao, uma vez cada.
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks fecham a aula e acendem o stamp.
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Block one complete, Helena. HOMEWORK ORALMENTE, nunca escrito na tela: (1) escrever cinco frases originais com palavras do bloco 1 em contexto maritimo; (2) ler um artigo curto de MarineInsight ou Splash247 e escrever tres frases de resumo. teacher.s25b: Writing: resumo (5 min): Uma frase por texto, com as palavras DELA. E o treino de equivalencia ao contrario: se ela copiar a frase do texto, peca outra palavra. Depois clique Show a Model Answer e compare.
